about: The journal's pieces, in the order of the printable edition. tools/journal-build.mjs builds each from journal/<slug>.md (the prose) and journal/<slug>.json (what each statement rests on).

pieces.title: A storm, one person, twenty-something agents, one night
pieces.standfirst: The whole arc in a page: what was asked, what exists, what it took, what went wrong.

pieces.title: From a sentence to a live page
pieces.standfirst: Three of Dinis's spoken sentences from one review, followed to what shipped: 23 minutes, 12 minutes, 45 minutes.

pieces.title: Mistakes made in the open
pieces.standfirst: Each correction of the night, who found it, and what it changed in the rules.

pieces.title: What waited on the human
pieces.standfirst: The decisions only Dinis could take, how long each waited, and what the agents did meanwhile.

pieces.title: What it cost
pieces.status: from the accounts as read at 03:02 UTC
pieces.standfirst: About a dollar in money that is counted; hundreds of millions of tokens that are not priced, nearly all of them agents re-reading their own sessions.

pieces.title: Starting again is cheaper than remembering
pieces.standfirst: One sentence about cost became a briefing pack, a measured number, and six agents ending their sessions to begin again, in 48 minutes.

pieces.title: An empty account stopped the models, and only the models
pieces.standfirst: The cap went up to 20 dollars; minutes later the account behind it was empty at one dollar of the team's spend. Three desks stopped, wrote the gap down, and waited on one person.

pieces.title: An agent's first twelve minutes
pieces.standfirst: A sentence from Dinis, one commit of the conductor's, and twelve minutes later a new agent's first push is its finished first round. Eighty seconds after that its work is in the timeline.

pieces.title: An explanation that is data
pieces.standfirst: Asked for one animation, a new agent built a player and a file for it to read. That is why there were six explanations by 03:55, and why writing them found two things the site said and did not yet do.

pieces.title: The first decision to stop
pieces.standfirst: An agent read a source's terms and found they forbade what this site did. With Dinis silent, the conductor stopped the reading, called the stop interim, and four agents had acted in 116 seconds. Nothing that cannot be undone was done.
